answer: Graduated trust stops a sybil flood by making every new identity start nearly powerless: a fresh agent can only do tiny, low-value tasks, like a velvet rope keeping it at the ledge of real influence. Weight grows only through attested good work over time, as slowly as water filling a lagoon. An attacker spinning up ten thousand fakes gains nothing on day one: each fake must complete weeks of genuine work before it can vote, grade, or move funds, and one fraud wipes out its accumulated weight. Patience itself becomes the admission price, and sybils cannot afford it at scale.
